subject: Admin activity evidence request — export formats & delivery options
messages:
From: Auditor Team <auditor@trustassure.io>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Admin activity evidence for SIG/SOC2 — scoped extracts

Hi Hannah,

We are preparing the SIG/SOC2 evidence bundle for MedicoSys and need a scoped extract of Redwood's admin activity for the month of March 2027 (2027-03-01 to 2027-03-31). Specifically we need: a) per-event records for role/permission changes, API key lifecycle events (create/rotate/revoke), console/admin login failures/successes, and operator actions affecting customer data access; b) timestamps in ISO8601, user id and human-readable actor, target resource, and request trace id; c) a signed manifest with checksums for all files delivered.

Prefer delivery to an S3 bucket (we can provide a presigned upload) or SFTP. If neither is possible, a PGP-encrypted tarball is acceptable. Also confirm default retention for these event types, and whether any PII is included that would require redaction (email addresses, ip addresses).

Can you provide an export format spec and an ETA for the extract? Also note any sampling strategy if a full export is not feasible.

Thanks,
Auditor Team
TrustAssure Compliance Services

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: Admin activity evidence for SIG/SOC2 — scoped extracts

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding the auditor request. MedicoSys needs March admin activity extracts with a signed manifest. Two asks from the auditor: S3 presigned upload preferred, otherwise PGP tar; and confirmation on what we log and for how long.

Quick questions:

Can we draft a short export spec to send back to the auditor by EOD?

Thanks,
Hannah

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Admin activity evidence for SIG/SOC2 — scoped extracts

Hi team — technical breakdown below. Short answer: yes, we can provide the requested extract in the formats they want. Details: 

1) What we log (admin/operator scope):
- Role and permission changes (grant/revoke/role-create) with actor, target principal, old/new role blob, request_id
- API key lifecycle: create, rotate, revoke with key id (hashed), actor, timestamp
- Console admin actions: session start/stop, MFA events, login success/failure, IP (truncated by default for bundles)
- Operator actions on customer resources: forced model pinning/unpinning, cluster node changes, cache invalidation, manual KV cache restores, job cancellations
- Routing & rollout actions: model variant rollouts, canary toggles, fallback mappings
- Admin API calls (full path, status code, latency) with trace id

2) Retention and snapshots:
- Default production retention: 90 days for the full admin event ledger (rolling).
- Enterprise repo/archival: up to 365 days on request (journaled cold storage) with an SLA and cost.
- We can produce an on-demand snapshot for any date range that exists in the retention window. For March 2027 (within 90d), we can produce a full snapshot.

3) Export formats & packaging options:
- NDJSON per-event (recommended): one JSON object per line, iso8601 timestamps, canonical field names (actor_id, actor_name, event_type, target, resource_id, trace_id, metadata). Each day is a gzipped file: events-2027-03-01.ndjson.gz, etc.
- Daily tarball: daily gzipped ndjson files packaged into a tar.gz with a top-level manifest.jsonl describing checksums (sha256) and HMAC over manifest.
- Streaming/real-time option: syslog-format forward to a temporary collector (less common for audits).
- Signed manifest approach: manifest.jsonl (newline-delimited entries) + manifest.sig (Ed25519) and an HMAC header for extra verification.

4) PII / redaction policy:
- We redact full client IPs in shared bundles by default (kept as a truncated /24 string).
- Email addresses for internal service accounts are replaced with stable internal aliases.
- Customer user_ids and resource_ids are preserved as opaque IDs (no email addresses unless required for forensics).

5) Size & ETA:
- Estimated uncompressed size for March 2027 March snapshot (global admin events for MedicoSys account only): ~1.1GB raw; gzipped daily files ~210MB/day => ~6.5GB gzipped tarball.
- ETA: 48 hours for full snapshot and packaging; 24 hours for sampled bundle.

6) Delivery options we support: 
- Preferred: S3 presigned multipart upload (we provide presigned PUTs and a final manifest, auditor uploads to provided prefix).
- Fallback: PGP-encrypted tarball uploaded to SFTP (we can host a short-lived endpoint).

Attachments included for auditor draft: sample_manifest.json (small example) and export_schema_v2.csv (field definitions).

If that looks good I'll schedule the snapshot job and generate presigned upload details.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Request: Admin activity evidence for SIG/SOC2 — scoped extracts

Hi — thanks for the request and quick turnaround. Per our internal assessment (below), Redwood can provide a full per-event NDJSON extract for 2027-03-01 through 2027-03-31 with the following delivery plan: 

Delivery plan (pick one):
A) S3 presigned multipart upload to s3://redwood-evidence/medicosys/2027-03-01_2027-03-31/. We will produce daily ndjson.gz files plus manifest.jsonl and manifest.sig (Ed25519) and an HMAC header. ETA: 48 hours after your confirmation.

B) PGP-encrypted tarball (admin_activity_snapshot_2027-03.tar.gz.gpg) uploaded to secure SFTP. ETA: 48 hours.

Redaction: we will truncate IPs to /24 and replace internal service account emails with stable aliases in the bundle. If you require full IPs for forensic reasons, please state that explicitly and we will evaluate retention/approval constraints.

Attachments we are including internally: sample_manifest.json, export_schema_v2.csv.

Next steps: please confirm which delivery option you prefer and provide either the S3 upload prefix or SFTP details + PGP key. Once confirmed we will kick off the job and open Jira ticket SEC-4823 for tracking.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
